raw_emails:
From: Lucas Moreno <lucas@novum.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Unexpected metering spike on Novum integration

Hi Sean,

We noticed a sudden metering spike on Dec 1 that resulted in a ~3.7x increase on our December invoice (INV-20261201). Attached is a screenshot from our monitoring showing token counts by hour. Can you help us understand where these extra tokens came from?

A few details that may help:
- Integration: batch ingestion endpoint (v2) from our EU cluster
- Expected pattern: 120k tokens/day average, peak ~180k
- Billed: ~640k tokens on Dec 1

We'd like an itemized breakdown (per-request token counts) and any evidence of retries/duplicate submissions on Redwood's side. Also need confirmation on VAT treatment for the credit if one is issued — we are VAT-registered (EU).

Thanks,
Lucas
VP Engineering
Novum AI

Attachment: screenshot-metering-spike.png (png)

----------
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Moreno <lucas@novum.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Unexpected metering spike on Novum integration

Hi Lucas —

Sorry to hear about the surprise on your invoice. I'm looping in Marissa from Billing and Ben, your account lead, so we can investigate and get you a clear response.

Initial notes from a quick look:
- Our metering system counts tokens at the point of server-side receipt. Duplicate client resends can show as additional tokens if requests were re-submitted.
- We sometimes see spikes when parallel workers requeue with overlapping prefixes (common with large batch ingestion).
- Dec 1 shows three short bursts between 03:14–03:23 UTC that look anomalous compared to your typical hourly profile.

Next steps I'd like to propose:
1) Marissa will request the per-request token audit for Dec 1 and look for identical payload hashes / repeated client IPs.
2) We can provisionally flag the invoice while we complete the audit — that prevents collection actions and gives us time to validate.
3) If we confirm duplicate ingestion on our side or a server-side replay, we will issue a credit and confirm VAT handling.

I've attached a token log request template to speed things up — if you can share any client-side IDs (job IDs, request IDs) that would help correlate.

Thanks,
Sean
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: token-log-request.csv (csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Moreno <lucas@novum.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 14:27:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Unexpected metering spike on Novum integration

Hi Lucas —

Thanks for the detail and the screenshot. We ran a targeted audit for Dec 1 (per your invoice INV-20261201) and wanted to share findings and a recommended resolution. Summary first:

- Findings:
  * There were 3 concentrated bursts originating from the same client token (client_api_key ending ...x9f2).
  * For two of those bursts we observed repeated request digests with identical payloads and identical client IPs — consistent with a client-side retry loop.
  * One burst, however, shows a pattern where our routing proxy re-forwarded a small subset of requests after a transient upstream timeout. This resulted in ~42k tokens that match server-side replay signatures.

- Impact:
  * Of the ~520k additional tokens billed, approx 42k are attributable to a server-side replay. The remainder appears to be client retries.

- Proposed resolution:
  1) We will issue a discretionary credit for the server-side replay portion (42,000 tokens) on INV-20261201.
  2) For the remaining overage, we can provide the per-request logs to help Novum determine if client-side retry logic caused resubmission; if you confirm those were unintentional we can consider a goodwill adjustment.

VAT handling: since Novum is VAT-registered in the EU, any credit will include an updated credit note reflecting the VAT reversal; please confirm your VAT registration number when you accept the credit so we can issue paperwork correctly.

I opened an internal ticket to improve replay protections on that routing proxy (RPROXY-2143). We've also attached the redacted per-request audit for Dec 1 so you can inspect request IDs and payload digests.

Let me know if you'd like us to apply the provisional credit now (we will show it as a negative line on your next statement) or wait until you complete your review.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: dec1_per_request_audit_redacted.csv (csv)
Link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/novum-billing-audit-2026-12

From: Lucas Moreno <lucas@novum.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@novum.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 16:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Unexpected metering spike on Novum integration

Marissa —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and for flagging RPROXY-2143. We reviewed the redacted audit and can confirm the two repeated request digests are indeed client-side retries from a failed batch job; we've pushed a fix to avoid duplicate submissions going forward.

We accept the discretionary credit for the 42,000 tokens attributable to Redwood's server-side replay. Our VAT registration number is GB999999973 (EU VAT). Please issue the credit note and updated invoice reflecting the VAT reversal.

One ask: before you apply the credit, can you provide the exact token-to-GBP conversion used on INV-20261201 and the math for the credit amount (so our finance team can reconcile)? Also confirm the credit will appear on our next statement and that no collection actions will be taken while this is open.

If you can send the credit note and the breakdown, we can close this ticket quickly. Appreciated.

—Lucas
VP Engineering, Novum AI
